identity.title: Orthogonal Subspace Decomposition for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

problem.claim: Improve detection of AI-generated natural and face images, which is important but challenging.

gap.claim: The authors identify failure to generalize as arising from detectors overfitting limited, monotonous fake patterns, constraining the feature space and limiting expressivity and generalization.

contributions.claim: An SVD-based orthogonal subspace decomposition that freezes principal components and adapts the remaining components to preserve pretrained knowledge while learning fake patterns.
An asymmetry-based account of why naive AIGI detectors fail to generalize.
A prior that fake images derive from real images and therefore exhibit a hierarchical rather than independent relationship.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents a new perspective on AIGI detection generalization failure and explicitly enforces orthogonality during tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the constrained, low-ranked feature space is proved to seriously limit expressivity and generalization.
Relative to full-parameter and LoRA-based tuning, the authors report that explicit orthogonality enables a higher-rank overall feature space and minimizes overfitting while enhancing generalization.
The authors report identifying a learned prior that fakes are derived from real images, suggesting a hierarchical relationship.

narrative_sequence.summary: AIGI detection is important yet challenging.
The authors attribute generalization failure to asymmetric overfitting of limited fake patterns and a resulting low-ranked feature space.
They propose combining pretrained foundation-model knowledge with SVD decomposition into orthogonal subspaces, freezing principal components and adapting the remainder.
They distinguish the method from full-parameter and LoRA tuning through explicit orthogonality, then identify a real-to-fake hierarchical prior as important for generalization.
Implementation code is reported as publicly available.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a specific failure mechanism—overfitting fake patterns and low feature-space rank—to a structural intervention that preserves principal components and adapts orthogonal residual components.

lessons.interpretation: A mechanism-to-design mapping can make a method’s motivation and claimed benefit easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a generalization method, explicitly connect the diagnosed representation failure to the component or constraint introduced to address it.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed intervention is not designed around a stated failure mechanism or when the mechanism is only speculative.

source_observation.claim: The abstract states both a comparison target—full-parameter and LoRA tuning—and the distinguishing property of the proposed method: explicit orthogonality.

lessons.interpretation: Naming the comparison axis and differentiating property sharpens a contribution claim.
lessons.application: Frame comparisons around the precise property that supposedly changes the outcome, then state the reported directional effect.
lessons.exception: Do not use this pattern to imply superiority when the source provides no comparative result or conditions.

unknowns: No quantitative results, datasets, evaluation protocols, or implementation details are provided.
The conditions and basis for the reported proof of limitation are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish whether the claimed generalization improvements hold across particular generators, domains, or tuning settings.
